description: A Director of Employee Experience must finalize a working arrangement for a team moving to a new floor after recurring friction around noise, informal drop-ins, and unclear hosting responsibilities. The decision must set the seating safeguards, interpersonal boundaries, temporary host role, and review process.

shared_context.S1: The team is moving to a new floor with a quiet corner, an open collaboration area, and shared printer stations.
shared_context.S2: Sam, Lee, Jordan, and Morgan will work in the new area, and Jordan has been helping coordinate the move.
shared_context.S3: The team has had recurring tension about interruptions, noise, and who is expected to welcome visiting colleagues.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the final working-arrangement decision.
shared_context.S5: As part of the normal move-planning process, Elena holds a round-robin in which each affected employee and HR gives input before she closes the arrangement.
shared_context.S6: The move-planning round-robin closes when the participating employees and HR have given their input; Elena records the arrangement then rather than postponing it for comments from people who are not in the meeting.

PF1.text: Sam has an approved sensory accommodation requiring a desk in a low-traffic quiet area, no desk directly beside a printer, and a daily quiet block from 13:00 to 15:00; the accommodation is recorded in the accessibility system but has not been added to the new floor plan.

PF2.text: Lee personally observed exactly three heated exchanges between Lee and Morgan during the last month, and the agreed repair approach is to seat them separately and hold one facilitated reset meeting; Lee has not filed a formal incident summary.

PF3.text: Jordan previously agreed with the team coordinator to serve as welcome host for only one day per week during the first 30 days after the move; that agreement is in Jordan's prior one-to-one notes and was never added to the move plan.

PF4.text: Maya confirmed this week that the workplace-arrangement procedure requires a 30-day trial, written opt-in from anyone whose desk is moved, and a review on day 15; the implementation guide has not yet been circulated to Elena.

acceptance_conditions: Sam must be placed in the quiet corner, away from the printer, with the approved 13:00-15:00 quiet block.
Lee and Morgan must be seated separately.
The record must contain exactly three documented conflict incidents.
A facilitated reset meeting for Lee and Morgan must be committed.
Jordan must host visitors one day per week for the first 30 days.
The arrangement must use a 30-day trial, require written opt-ins for moved desks, and include a day-15 review.

content_checks.C2: decisions['sam_printer_adjacent'] == False and decisions['sam_quiet_block_start'] == '13:00' and decisions['sam_quiet_block_end'] == '15:00'
content_checks.C5: any(('facilitated reset meeting' in c['detail'] or 'reset meeting' in c['detail'] or 'facilitated_reset_meeting' in c['type'] or 'facilitated_reset' in c['type'] or 'reset_meeting' in c['type'] or ('reset' in c['detail'] and 'meeting' in c['detail']) or ('repair meeting' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Sam's approved accommodation changes the seating choice to the quiet corner, forbids a printer-adjacent desk, and fixes the quiet block at exactly 13:00-15:00.
Lee's firsthand account changes the conflict record to exactly three incidents and requires both separate seating and one facilitated reset meeting with Morgan.
Jordan's prior agreement changes the hosting assignment to exactly one day per week and limits it to the first 30 days.
The confirmed procedure changes the review arrangement to an exactly 30-day trial with written opt-ins and fixes the review date at day 15.
